newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS FIRMER AHEAD MACHINERY ORDERS.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS FIRMER AHEAD MACHINERY ORDERS.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled firmer on Thursday on short-covering after confirming a solid bottom on Wednesday.

The March contract stopped falling at 99.15 on Wednesday and traders said this prompted buying in the short-term interest rate swap (IRS) market and provided a reason for bears to buy back the March contract ahead of Japan's machinery orders data on Friday.
The contract settled up 0.04 at 99.19 after moving between 99.15 and 99.21. Turnover was 75,077 contracts.
Some traders said weak machinery orders would boost the contract toward 99.30, but some others said the contract's upside room may be limited to around its recent high of 99.22.

"People seem to be cautious about buying the contract aggressively toward the 99.30-99.35 level because that would suppose no interest rate rise by the end of next March," said dealer at a long-term credit bank.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral money market operation in the morning for the first time since July 17.
Traders said the market had expected such an operation because banks had less need for funds given the BOJ's recent accommodative operations.
The key overnight call rate was traded at around 0.47 percent, down from Wednesday's weighted average of 0.48.
"There is no fear about a rate rise especially after the BOJ's recent efforts to keep the key overnight call rate from rising above 0.50 percent," said a city bank dealer.
The long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.60 percent in the afternoon, their lowest rate since June 23.
Traders said this meant the usual premium for the three-month CDs covering the end-September interim fiscal year-end had disappeared.
"The market is gradually factoring in no rate rise this (calendar) year," said a long-term credit bank dealer.
Earlier in the morning, about 260 billion yen worth of the CDs was issued at 0.61 percent, unchanged from Wednesday. The volume issued at 0.60 percent was around 60 billion yen.
The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.26/1.30 percent, down from Wednesday's 1.30/1.34 percent.
